statement: By writing $\cos5\theta+\cos\theta$ as a product, or otherwise, solve $\cos5\theta+\cos\theta=0$ for $0\le\theta<\pi$.
solution: Using $\cos A+\cos B=2\cos\tfrac{A+B}{2}\cos\tfrac{A-B}{2}$: $\cos5\theta+\cos\theta=2\cos3\theta\cos2\theta$. Setting this to zero gives $\cos3\theta=0$ or $\cos2\theta=0$. For $0\le\theta<\pi$, $\cos3\theta=0$ gives $3\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{2},\tfrac{5\pi}{2}$, so $\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{6},\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$; and $\cos2\theta=0$ gives $2\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{2}$, so $\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{4},\tfrac{3\pi}{4}$. The solutions are $\theta=\tfrac{\pi}{6},\tfrac{\pi}{4},\tfrac{\pi}{2},\tfrac{3\pi}{4},\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$.
hints: Set each cosine factor to zero.
